record.original_question: Is the intersection of two finitely generated ideals in H ∞ finitely generated? (L. A. Rubel)

evidence.quote: Is the intersection of two finitely generated ideals in H ∞ finitely generated? (L. A. Rubel)
For H ∞ (D), an affirmative answer was given by McVoy and Rubel [559]. This was extended to any finitely connected domain by Barnard (no ci- tation).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H^\infty = H^\infty(\mathbb{D})$ denote the Banach algebra of bounded holomorphic functions on the open unit disc $\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$, equipped with pointwise addition and multiplication and the supremum norm. An ideal $I \subseteq H^\infty$ is called finitely generated if there exist $f_1, \dots, f_n \in H^\infty$ such that $I = \{g_1 f_1 + \cdots + g_n f_n : g_1, \dots, g_n \in H^\infty\}$. 

Determine whether the following holds: for any two finitely generated ideals $I, J \subseteq H^\infty$, the intersection $I \cap J$ is again a finitely generated ideal of $H^\infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: McVoy and Rubel proved that the intersection of two finitely generated ideals in H^∞(D) is finitely generated, giving an affirmative answer to Rubel's question. Barnard extended this to any finitely connected domain.
